title: Converge premerge notifier, lightweight lint adapter, and slim release hook refactor
author: Leah Kim
description:
Context: Our premerge notification landscape is fragmented: webhooks, separate alerting lambdas, and a verbose release hook that duplicates status logic. This causes noisy signals during large rollout windows and makes it hard to reason about which premerge checks actually blocked a change. Motivation: simplify signal paths, reduce duplicate work, and enable a lightweight adapter for TypeScript lint runners so premerge feedback is faster and less resource-intensive.

What this PR does: consolidates notification logic into a single premerge-notifier service (batched fanout, idempotent state), introduces a small typescript lint-adapter that runs only changed-file linters for fast feedback, and refactors the release hook to call the notifier (instead of reimplementing status aggregation).

Scope and non-goals: this PR focuses on orchestration and adapter interfaces; it intentionally avoids changing runtime lint rules. It does not touch dedicated capacity autoscaling or the on-prem installer.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement batched notifier server + idempotent queue consumer
- [x] Add minimal TS lint adapter and wiring for changed-file detection
- [x] Swap release-hook invocation to notifier (replace duplicate logic)
- [x] Add feature flag: ci.premerge_converge (default: enabled for ci namespace)
- [x] E2E smoke test pipeline and unit tests for adapter interfaces
- [x] Update docs: /docs/ci/premerge-notifier.md and premerge runbook

Rollout plan: merge behind feature flag; enable for ci-owned repos for 48h; monitor premerge latency and notification duplicate count (new metrics: premerge.notifier.latency, premerge.notifier.duplicates). If regressions detected, roll back flag and revert via release automation.

Backwards compat: notifier respects existing payloads for webhooks and exposes a compatibility shim. Integrations that call the old release hook continue to work for one release cycle.

Testing done: unit coverage for batched fanout, integration test between GitHub webhook shim => notifier => lint-adapter. Performed a staged rollout to ci/* repos and validated lower median premerge feedback time (~35% improvement) and 60% reduction in duplicate notifications.
